provenance.note: Measured at load 1.98 after the NCC hot-loop change (b1d74bf): four accumulator chains in prepare_chip! and integral_both!, ifelse for the denominator guard, FFTW_PATIENT plans. This run carries the CPU-time column, which exists because two earlier readings of this table were wrong without it. Wall clock is work divided by parallelism achieved; CPU time is the work. On a shared machine only the latter is comparable across runs. The change is a real win at both thread counts, from an interleaved A/B against its parent b4fb528 -- two reps, alternating base/HEAD so a load spike cannot land on one side, identical 920544 points: 1 thread 75.6 -> 68.6 s CPU (9.3% less work, wall 74.1 -> 67.0), 12 threads 89.7 -> 82.2 s CPU (8.4% less, wall 22.2 -> 21.6). Both reproduce to within 0.3 s. Two retracted claims, recorded so neither is re-derived. First: that the 12-thread wall clock (33-35 s at load 2.7-3.5) was contention. Second: that a non-interleaved A/B showed the change 1.03x SLOWER threaded. The first was right in substance and dismissed too early; the second was the artifact -- its base and HEAD runs were not interleaved, so a load spike biased one side. At load 1.98 this row is 21.3 s at 3.83 cores, faster than the 8d7c1ec run's 25.6 s, so the ~2.85 cores seen at higher load was the machine and not a lost-parallelism regression. The 4096 lazy row peaked at 9537 MiB against 3599 at 2048: 25 blocks on 12 threads holds twelve 6144-pixel working sets at once, which measures the block size being large relative to the scene rather than what blocking costs. 8192 is excluded for the same reason at 9 blocks.
